findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed a large container of cooked fried rice stored at room temperature without marking indicating when it must be discarded. The PIC stated they take the rice out when it’s busy and put it back inside the cooler when it’s not busy. The inspector educated about temperature abuse and the importance of either using time-as-control (TAC) or only bringing out small amounts of food that can be used during lunch/dinner rushes. The PIC stated that the rice was cooked at 12 pm and thus must be discarded at 4 pm. The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to ensure that the facility is marking the four hour window for TAC or only pulling out small amounts of cooked fried rice that can be used within lunch/dinner rushes.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed there was chicken and shrimp thawing at room temperature when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that the chicken and shrimp were recently removed from the freezer. The chicken and shrimp were immediately moved into the walk-in cooler. Temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must always be thawed according to an approved method: (1) Within a cooler at 41F or less; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) In the microwave; or (4) As part of the cooking process. Ensure that TCS foods are always thawed properly to maintain food safety.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

3-501.15 Portion of recently cooked shrimp was observed with internal temperature of 68F in a stainless steel bowl in the top holding area of the prep cooler. One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Beef is thawing at room temperature. Reference 3-501.13.
